stances.summary: Democrats positioned to gain House seats from redistricting
stances.quote: Democrats just got one seat closer to retaking the House (by Eli McKown-Dawson). Missouri’s new old map has diminished Republicans’ redistricting gains.

stances.summary: Cautions against overweighting polling swings in midterm forecasts
stances.quote: Beware big swings in midterm forecasts. As Labor Day approaches, we’re entering the traditional stretch run of the campaign. But history says the national picture probably won’t change much before Election Day.

stances.summary: Democrats likely to govern more Americans than Republicans
stances.quote: A tour of the 9 key governor races (by Eli McKown-Dawson). Democrats are almost certain to govern more Americans than Republicans, but can they flip swing states like Georgia?

stances.summary: Expresses qualified skepticism about Texas turning blue
stances.quote: Do I really buy that Texas could turn blue?. Some of the skepticism about James Talarico’s chances amounts to superstition. But I have one lingering concern about our forecast in Texas.

stances.summary: Democrats advantaged in Northeast, Midwest, West races
stances.quote: A tour of the 48 key House races (by Eli McKown-Dawson). In the Northeast, Midwest and West, it’s almost all upside for Democrats. But redistricting will hand Republicans some seats in the South.

stances.summary: Questions whether Democratic polling strength is sustainable
stances.quote: Are Democrats on a summer sugar high?. They’re polling surprisingly strongly in some Senate races. But should you bet on those numbers falling back to earth? Plus, some quick thoughts on Alaska and Florida.

stances.summary: Democratic resistance candidates underperformed in primaries; voters want to move on
stances.quote: It's kind of been a rough set of primaries for Heroes of the Resistance 1.0 between Vindman losing tonight, Dan Goldman losing his seat (although there were other issues there) and George Conway getting only 6% of the vote in NY-12. People want to move on.

stances.summary: Frames Ossoff and Kamala as joint threats to Newsom in Democratic primary
stances.quote: Ossoff and Kamala are like a pincer movement to Newsom in these D primary polls.

stances.summary: Characterizes Ossoff as more viable than Newsom despite less name recognition
stances.quote: Kamala's getting the voters who just want to run it back for some inexplicable reason. And Ossoff's getting the Telegenic White Guy Who Fights vote, but has actually won in a swing state before and is newer and more exciting.

stances.summary: Vindman was overconfident candidate choice due to lack of Florida ties
stances.quote: Prediction markets have flipped from Vindman ~92% at the start of the night to Nixon ~95% now. That 92% was probably overconfident given the lack of info on the race and that Vindman is kind of a shitty candidate because of his lack of Florida ties.

stances.summary: Democrats struggle to nominate competitive candidates in deeper red states like Florida
stances.quote: General election polls have had Nixon doing a bit worse than Vindman vs. Moody, and Vindman wasn't doing well. She has raised $1M to Vindman's $16M and is a DSA member. Democrats continue to struggle to nominate candidates who are good matches for Florida.

stances.summary: Prediction markets have limitations beyond polling and models
stances.quote: Prediction markets aren't magic. My chat with Galen Druke on Wisconsin, models, polls and prediction markets.

stances.summary: Criticizes slow vote counting in California as procedurally ridiculous
stances.quote: Since this election is settled this hopefully won't take on too much of a partisan valence but can we just agree it's ridiculous that it takes California several weeks to count its votes? Imagine if it were a swing state.

stances.summary: Suggests Harris could perform well on Rogan's platform
stances.quote: Kamala should still go on Rogan, I bet she'd be pretty funny now that the pressure is off.

stances.summary: Criticizes Democratic primary process for renominating unpopular elderly candidate
stances.quote: You don't demonstrate your seriousness that Trump is an existential threat to democracy by going through the motions to renominate an 81-year-old with a 38% approval rating who 75% of voters think is too old without giving anyone a choice because that's just how things are done.

stances.summary: Notes Democratic primary voters ignored elite liberal opposition to Biden
stances.quote: Sorry if this is a bit random, but the fact that Biden easily won the Democratic primary despite having little support from blue-checkmark liberal elites is something that ought to have been a pretty big wake-up call but doesn't seem to have been.

stances.summary: Highlights Democratic significance of Georgia Senate runoff victories
stances.quote: It's for extremely understandable reasons, but people seem to be sleeping on the significance of the fact that Democrats **just won two runoffs in Georgia** to **claim control of Congress**.

stances.summary: Rates Republican election outcome as severe and warns of Trump's damaging legacy
stances.quote: I'm too tired for long takes but on a scale from 0 to 10 on how bad this is for the GOP, it's maybe like a 9, not just because of the immediate implications, but also because it may imply that Trump is sort of a poison pill for how the party navigates its future.

stances.summary: Predicts Hawley will underperform despite pundit hype as GOP frontrunner
stances.quote: Hawley seems like the sort of politician who will be heralded by pundits as the new GOP frontrunner in some future election year and then will finish in 5th place in Iowa.

stances.summary: Criticizes media narrative spinning Democratic election win as loss
stances.quote: Feels like everyone's running with their Why-Democrats-Lost takes even though Democrats won.

stances.summary: Defends probabilistic forecasting against criticism of pre-election predictions
stances.quote: There's this dumb argument circulating that if you'd known in advance what would happen—i.e. Trump beating his polls—you shouldn't have Biden e.g. a 90% chance of winning. Actually, if you'd known in advance what would happen, you should have given Biden a 100% chance of winning!

stances.summary: Condemns Trump operatives for hypocrisy on accepting election calls
stances.quote: So Trump operatives are bragging about how the news media has called Alaska and North Carolina for them... while refusing to accept that the same news organization have called Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Nevada and the presidency for Biden. https://t.co/uSzTNjLsz3

stances.summary: Questions whether GOP leaders strategically promote election lies or truly believe them
stances.quote: It's hard to tell whether GOP leaders are being strategic and cynical (e.g. hoping to keep their base excited) when indulging claims of election-rigging, or are just wholly disconnected from reality. But in some ways I wonder if it's even possible to distinguish between the two.

stances.summary: Notes Trump's performance inferior to Clinton's despite similar Electoral margins
stances.quote:
Anybody who's like "we'll that was a pretty good showing for Trump!" should consider how Hillary Clinton was treated as the World's Biggest Loser after an election with the same Electoral College margin as this one*.

* But where she won the popular vote instead of losing it by 5

stances.summary: Argues delaying race calls enables presidential misinformation spreading
stances.quote: I don't know, but it sure seems to me like not calling the race when the outcome is obvious in states like PA and NV gives the president more time to spout misinformation.

stances.summary: Assesses Trump's Arizona chances diminishing
stances.quote: Those Maricopa ballots have probably closed down Trump's path in Arizona. He needed to do much better.

stances.summary: Network speed to call races affects credibility
stances.quote: Whichever network calls this first will look good in retrospect.

stances.summary: 2020 election notably uncompetitive by historical standards
stances.quote: Going by the popular vote, this will probably be the 2nd-least-close election since 2000.

stances.summary: Argues Nevada call is justified by ballot data
stances.quote: If 90% of the ballots are from Clark County, there's no reason not to call Nevada.

stances.summary: Emphasizes importance of Georgia runoff races for Senate control
stances.quote: I'm not sure it's really sunk in yet, even among reporters, that we're probably going to get 2 runoffs in Georgia on Jan. 5 that will determine control of the Senate.

stances.summary: Notes Trump dependent on post-Election Day ballots for comeback
stances.quote: Worth mentioning that if you stopped counting ballots *right now*, Biden would win with this map. So Trump is reliant on ballots counted after Election Day for his comeback chances. https://t.co/rGQQT3X2Ub

stances.summary: Suggests remaining Michigan votes likely favor Biden
stances.quote: Michigan now tied and there's every reason to think the remaining votes will be pretty blue.

stances.summary: Warns against premature election result interpretation
stances.quote:
Those warnings we gave you about not paying too much attention to results until you're sure a county is fully reported... you're already ignoring them!

But I'll say it again: don't pay much attention to results until you're sure a county is fully reported (mail, in-person, etc.)

stances.summary: Warns against early election result analysis before counting complete
stances.quote: You're not going to learn anything useful about the election outcome on here until 7pm, i.e. when they start counting votes.

stances.summary: Warns against media efforts to create false ambiguity around clear election outcome
stances.quote: I'm too tired to make this point eloquently, but part of what happens at the end of a not-especially-close election is that there's a lot of effort to create ambiguity, and you have to be pretty steadfast to see through that ambiguity.

stances.summary: Frames Trump's premature victory claim as threat to democracy, not media story
stances.quote: Tired of people framing "Trump will declare victory prematurely" as a media story. Most likely—in part because the White House has telegraphed it so much in advance—the media will be fairly well-prepared. Instead, it's a story about Trump seeking to undermine faith in democracy.

stances.summary: Notes Trump's messaging weak amid COVID and stock market decline
stances.quote: I don't want to be too snarky but Trump needs to close a big polling deficit and this is the message on a day with 80k new COVID cases and a 940 point decline in the Dow.

stances.summary: Notes Trump's campaign incompetence undercuts historical re-election models
stances.quote: Trump can still win. But on the other hand, if you're deriving a model from history, it implicitly presumes some baseline level of competence from a presidental campaign that may not be compatible with, say, getting into a public spat with Dr. Fauci 3 weeks out from the election.

stances.summary: Implies Lindsey Graham avoids COVID testing to protect Barrett nomination
stances.quote: Repeating myself and others here, but the reason Lindsey Graham won't get tested despite having been exposed to many COVID+ people is because if he reveals a positive test and has to quarantine the Amy Coney Barrett nomination could get scuttled. There is no other logical reason.

stances.summary: Critiques Trump for rejecting stimulus that would aid his re-election
stances.quote: Wait, so Trump not only rejects stimulus funds that would probably have helped his re-election chances, but *also* does so in a way to make sure that he personally will take blame for it?

stances.summary: Questions Trump debate strategy given polling deficit
stances.quote: I'm not sure why trying to fight the debate to a messy, unwatchable draw is supposed to be a good strategy for Trump when he's 7 points behind in the polls.

stances.summary: Argues Trump tax disclosure refusal undercuts 'fake news' claims
stances.quote: Sorry if this point is a little obvious, but it's pretty hard for Trump to sustain an argument that the NYT taxes story is "fake news" when he won't release his taxes himself. Obviously the base will buy it but I'm not sure that anybody else does.

stances.summary: Assesses Trump losing badly with limited time for recovery
stances.quote: You don't need a fancy algorithm to know that Trump is losing, pretty badly at the moment. The Supreme Court pick doesn't seem to be helping him. The COVID situation may be getting worse again. Maybe the debates will help. But the clock is ticking: people are already voting.

stances.summary: Expresses alarm at unspecified concerning development
stances.quote: OK this is real bad tho

stances.summary: Harris as VP pick benefits Biden in California
stances.quote: I'm guessing that Biden will win California now with this Harris pick.

stances.summary: Criticizes Warren critics' inconsistency
stances.quote: I'm not trying to piss people off but it's a little rich that some prominent voices who spent months saying how awful Warren was compared to Bernie are now furious at Warren for failing to endorse him.

stances.summary: Sanders as frontrunner based on state wins and polling
stances.quote: Personally, I'd say the candidate who won 1.5 states (Sanders) is the frontrunner over the candidate who won 0.5 states (Buttigieg), especially if that candidate is also leading national polls.

stances.summary: Media coverage disproportionately favors lower-placing candidates
stances.quote: So apparently the candidate in 3rd place is a bigger story than the candidate in 2nd place, who in turn is a bigger story than the candidate in 1st place? OK.

stances.summary: Media should cover frontrunner more than second and third place
stances.quote: I know a Sanders win is somewhat priced in, but I'm not sure why the story is about who finishes in 2nd and 3rd place instead of him winning, especially if it looks like a decently clear win.

stances.summary: Criticizes Iowa and New Hampshire for lacking demographic diversity
stances.quote: If the Democratic Party wants a field that's representative of its members and its voters, it probably shouldn't have two states as white as Iowa and New Hampshire vote first every year.

stances.summary: Celebrates Buttigieg's historic nomination candidacy
stances.quote:
Just want to get this out of the way so I only have to say it once:

It's a big deal that an openly gay man is a serious contender for a major party's presidential nomination, and if you're liberal who wants to equivocate about that too much, you can pretty much fuck right off.

stances.summary: Highlights underreported Democratic turnout strength
stances.quote:
About 60 million people turned out to vote for Democrats for the House this year. That is a **crazy** number. (Republicans got 45m votes in the 2010 wave.)

And this was sort of missed. Why so many stories about Trump voters in truck stops and not so many about "the resistance"?

stances.summary: Condemns Trump's election delegitimization as authoritarian
stances.quote: The recent rhetoric from Trump, and often other Republicans, trying to delegitimize election results is awfully dangerous. Maybe the most openly authoritarian move he's made so far.

stances.summary: Warns Trump will escalate xenophobic rhetoric if Republicans gain
stances.quote: If Republicans have a good night on Tuesday and think they won the midterm on the basis of immigration/xenophobia/race-baiting, just imagine how much Trump is going to turn the dial up in 2020.

stances.summary: Uncertainty about popular vote parallels Electoral College disputes
stances.quote: If we don't know if Clinton really won the popular vote then we also don't know if Trump really won the Electoral College. https://t.co/ifZq7tALDy

stances.summary: Highlights Electoral College implications of gendered voting patterns
stances.quote: Exclusive @FiveThirtyEight projection on what the Electoral College would look like if women refuse to vote Trump. https://t.co/kmjxmjnY1l

stances.summary: Critiques TV news as low-value medium, questions gatekeeping on TV jobs
stances.quote: TV news is an extremely weird medium, even as compared to other media. The closest analogy is to acting. I don't think it contributes much value. But "only people with TV experience should get TV jobs" is just such a weird position for any sort of professional writer to defend.

stances.summary: Criticizes resistance media for covering trivial stories over substantive news
stances.quote: Ok maybe my tweet yesterday should have been more direct: too many of the Resistance newsletters focus on the stupidest possible shit. Yes, *this* is important/newsworthy. But there's so much about the fucking reflecting pool and FIFA and the WHCD and the White House ballroom.

stances.summary: Accuses journalists of suppressing lab-leak discussion due to partisan bias
stances.quote: This is so refreshingly honest. The Bad People thought the lab leak might be true, therefore as journalists we couldn't be expected to actually evaluate the evidence for it. https://t.co/NueOdLLAol

stances.summary: Questions framing of Trump unity message in NYT headline
stances.quote:
Tomorrow's NYT print edition.

Not sure "TRUMP URGES UNITY VS. RACISM" is how I would have framed the story. https://t.co/quOibXsp32

stances.summary: Demands accountability for 2016 election reporting failures
stances.quote: I’m not trying to be a jerk but the Times still owes its readers an explanation about what the f*** was going on with this vector of its reporting in 2016. https://t.co/YKGzEvyK8g

stances.summary: Criticizes columnist for trivializing serious politics
stances.quote: Imagine being a political columnist who could write about literally any topic you wanted and, given everything going on in American politics these days, you decided to write about how a woman member of Congress used a swear word.

stances.summary: Calls for proportionate coverage, acknowledges 2016 email bias
stances.quote: If you're one of those news organizations that treated Clinton's private emails like they were a national emergency, the solution isn't to treat Ivanka's private emails like they're also a national emergency—rather, it's to acknowledge that you kinda fucked up on Clinton.

stances.summary: TV should feature subject-matter experts, not generalist commentators
stances.quote: This is obvious I guess, but if you want to cut down on bothsidesism, put people on TV who have subject-matter expertise acquired through reporting or research... not generalists who are asked to opine on a whole bunch of topics they don't really know anything about.

stances.summary: Advocates for scientific polling over anecdotal interviews
stances.quote: What if—and hear me out because this will sound CRAZY—instead of interviewing a few voters at a time in a bar in Pennsylvania, we interviewed HUNDREDS of voters, chosen at random from all around the country. Furthermore, we'd ask them all the same questions to minimize bias.

stances.summary: Blames media's false balance for excessive email coverage
stances.quote: One shouldn't underrate how much the media's obsession with Clinton's emails stemmed from its obsession with fending off accusations of liberal bias. Trump had...  LOTS of issues.... so there was tremendous weight put on this one Clinton issue to preserve "balance". https://t.co/

stances.summary: Criticizes citing outlier polls as sign of bad faith
stances.quote: When someone regularly cites outlier polls instead of the polling average it's an **extremely** reliable tell that they're a bullshitter.

stances.summary: Expresses enduring anger at 2016 email server coverage
stances.quote: Gotta be honest: On a night like tonight, I'm still pretty pissed at those journalists and news organizations which treated Hillary Clinton's email server as a matter of apocalyptic importance.

stances.summary: Condemns 2016 email obsession as worst media failure
stances.quote:
As Trump’s problems mount, the media’s obsession with Clinton’s email server–literally the most-covered issue of 2016–
looks worse & worse.

stances.summary: Criticizes unfocused opposition strategy, advocates selective issue prioritization
stances.quote:
A more accurate paraphrase:
1) Trump scandals are an extremely target-rich environment
2) The public has a limited attention span
3) "Focusing" on everything, everywhere, all at once has been a catastrophically failed strategy for 12 years
QED: you should pick your battles

stances.summary: Trump normalization complete; substantive issues drive unpopularity more than abstract framing
stances.quote: Democrats have been running on this "let's not normalize Trump thing" for 12 years and he got elected president twice. He's been normalized. He's super unpopular now because of big substantive non-abstract things like Iran and the economy that have a direct impact on people.

stances.summary: Economy and Iran are substantive swing-voter motivators; other controversies less electorally important
stances.quote: People have finite attention spans. The economy, Iran and maybe ICE is a more than sufficient list of issues to motivate swing voters. If you want to elevate an overlooked issue, there are things orders of magnitude more objectively important than the fucking reflection pool.

stances.summary: Dismisses Trump corruption scandal as minor among many others
stances.quote: Who fucking cares it's literally not even in the top 100 Trump corruption scandals

stances.summary: Argues Trump is unfit for presidency and exposes media dishonesty
stances.quote:
It's just so weird living through this real-life Emperor Has  No Clothes Moment.

He obviously shouldn't be president for 4 more years. Everyone knows this. It's incredibly revealing which people are willing to lie about it.

stances.summary: Warns Republicans against positioning as moderate alternative to Trump
stances.quote: After the past 48 hours, I would not want to be one of those Republicans like Josh Hawley who hitched my star to the notion that I could offer some kindler, gentler, smarter version of Trumpism.

stances.summary: Implies job security despite Trump administration changes
stances.quote: @DonaldJTrumpJr I'll still have a job on January 21st, though.

stances.summary: Criticizes Trump's COVID response messaging as politically unwise
stances.quote: I understand he wants to project strength, but polls show that a large majority of the public doesn't think Trump took COVID seriously and that colors their response to his illness. So even apart from putting Secret Service members in danger, etc., not sure it's wise politically.

stances.summary: Equates Trump misconduct with Weinstein but notes Trump's nomination
stances.quote: Hard to think of any difference between Weinstein & Trump other than one of them was his PARTY's NOMINEE FOR PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES.

stances.summary: Analyzes Trump's pattern of attacking female minority critics
stances.quote: So, it totally fits the pattern that Trump is attacking the mayor San Juan. She challenged him and she's a woman (and Hispanic, obviously.) https://t.co/DJ2mZQixU9

stances.summary: Trump has poor impulse control and is easily triggered
stances.quote: Alternative hypothesis: Trump has poor impulse control & is easily triggered, especially when being challenged (esp. by women & minorities).

stances.summary: Silicon Valley caught off-guard by data center backlash
stances.quote: Why does everyone hate data centers?. My chat with Jasmine Sun about what role data centers could play in the midterms, how the backlash caught Silicon Valley by surprise — and why Claude can be so weird.

stances.summary: Data center backlash driven by corporate distrust, not AI-risk fears
stances.quote:
Just published my interview with @jasminewsun on the data center backlash. 

She makes a key point here. It's much more about people not trusting the huge tech firms ("big corporation scary") than anything involving AI x-risk ("big model scary") or even necessarily job losses.

stances.summary: Dismisses content moderation debate as unproductive
stances.quote: Guys the moderation debate is boring. Nobody is learning anything at this point and we're gonna get a bunch of new data in November.

stances.summary: Practical user testing superior to formal AI evaluations
stances.quote: In practice almost all customers are going to evaluate LLMs by road testing rather than "evals" and they're almost certainly right to do so.

stances.summary: Questions whether AI math breakthroughs exceed human mathematician resource allocation
stances.quote: Another question I'd have about the AI math breakthroughs is how they compare to the results you would have gotten if you'd budgeted the same amount of resources on human mathematicians and created incentives for them to go super hard on proofs.

stances.summary: Argues AI labs should prioritize consumer-facing results over academic peer recognition
stances.quote: The AI math proofs are impressive. But also probably among the hardest things for normies to appreciate. Personally, I think the AI labs underweight the value of putting bandwidth into achieving results that impress normies as opposed to evals/people within the peer group.

stances.summary: Contends consumer AI applications drive public sentiment more than pure math
stances.quote: Of course, it's hard to say to what extent this reflects spiky capabilities rather than resource allocation decisions. But "AI discovers a new drug" or "AI invents a highly popular consumer product from scratch" probably has a >> impact on public sentiment than pure math.

stances.summary: AI tools helpful with domain expertise, risky without human expert oversight
stances.quote: In the midst of my 3rd big coding/model project since March. I just can't emphasize enough how much a) AI tools are very helpful to someone (me, I suppose) with relevant domain knowledge, but b) would likely produce extremely buggy models without a human expert in the loop.

stances.summary: Observes resurgence of progressive activism reminiscent of 2019 trend
stances.quote: Yeah I don't know why groups like this are endorsing political candidates. But IMO we're seeing an increase in circa 2019-style woke politics lately. I don't think we'll hit particularly close to the 2019 peak, but it's higher than the ~2025 floor.

stances.summary: Suggests left confidence in political trends may be partly justified
stances.quote: Some of it comes from increased confidence on the left that political trends are blowing in their favor again, which is not necessarily wrong. People haven't changed that much since 2019. The difference this time is that people who didn't like Woke 1 probably won't nod along.

stances.summary: DSA members downwardly mobile despite high education, culturally liberal
stances.quote: The DSA sweet spot: highly educated, downwardly mobile. Education and economic security are usually correlated. But where the relationship breaks down is fertile territory for the new left.

stances.summary: Dismisses defenders of current events as beyond redemption
stances.quote: It's not just stupid but cringe, we're past the point of no return where people defending what's going on are redeemable.

stances.summary: Defends Ocasio-Cortez's policy knowledge against critics
stances.quote: I don't know, I watch these clips where Ocasio-Cortez is supposedly making huge gaffes and it seems like her policy knowledge is...probably about on par with or maybe a bit ahead of the average member of Congress.

stances.summary: Praises Parkland students' political effectiveness, criticizes threatened pundits
stances.quote: The thing about the Parkland students isn't that they're always spot-on—they've had better and worse moments as communicators. But they're at least as effective at politics as most professional pundits who have done it for years. Naturally, that's very threatening to the pundits.

stances.summary: Identifies Palin as underappreciated Trump precursor
stances.quote: Sorry for the random aside but I feel like Sarah Palin is under-discussed as a predecessor/precedent for Trumpism.

stances.summary: Condemns scientists for suppressing lab-leak discussion and harming public health
stances.quote:
Welp. The behavior of a certain cadre of scientists who used every trick in the book to suppress discussion of this issue is something I'll never forget. A huge disservice to science and public health. They should be profoundly embarrassed.

https://t.co/nZqzjrvo8F

stances.summary: Criticizes vaccine policy response as severe cost-benefit error
stances.quote: 6 cases out of 7 million people. What a disaster. This is going to get people killed. And it's going to create more vaccine hesitancy. These people don't understand cost-benefit analysis. They keep making mistakes by orders of magnitude.

stances.summary: Expresses concern about rising US and European COVID case rates
stances.quote: I'm not some sort of COVID alarmist... I've tried to stay pretty even-keeled and have been burned by being too optimistic at times... but I find the rising case rates in the US (and for that matter also Europe) pretty worrisome right now.

stances.summary: Raises concerns about White House superspreader event risks
stances.quote: I don't want to speculate *too* much about the political ramifications of…this…but that there apparently was a superspreading event, and that there are photos from the event of people hanging out indoors and outdoors in close proximity without masks on, is not great for the WH.

stances.summary: Criticizes White House for failing to prevent foreseeable COVID risks
stances.quote: "RBG dies 6 weeks before the election and the ceremony at the White House to name her replacement turns into a COVID-19 superspreading event" is, on the one hand, a remarkably strange sequence of events, but on the other hand chock-full of foreseeable risks that went unprevented.

stances.summary: Questions Trump's quarantine responsibility
stances.quote: So... is Trump going to self-quarantine?

stances.summary: Questions Elon Musk's ventilator production during shortage
stances.quote: There's a shortage now, how many ventilators you making @elonmusk?

stances.summary: Academia's politicization responsible for public skepticism
stances.quote: So, over the past few decades: (1) academia has become much more "political" and more of a political monoculture, (2) public perceptions of academia have massively tanked. Have you ever paused to consider, Todd, that maybe this is academia's fault, at least a little bit?

stances.summary: Trump attacks academia in fertile political territory
stances.quote: Academia has also come under more attacks from the government and particularly the Trump administration. But the Trump administration is operating in fertile political territory because higher ed has gone from an institution people revere to one they're deeply skeptical about.

stances.summary: Dismisses superficial defenses of academia's direction
stances.quote: No doubt the causal chains are complicated. And to some degree self-reinforcing. But  "see ya later Chamberlin" (spelled wrong btw) sounds like freshman-year-bong-hit argumentation, not a serious attempt to reconcile with the situation.

stances.summary: Questions academic organizations endorsing in low-salience Democratic primary
stances.quote:
I think it would be reasonable for academic organizations to be "political" in advocating for things like academic freedom.

but idk why they're making endorsements in a Senate primary between two Democrats in a race where this isn't even like one of the top 1000 issues.

stances.summary: Reports declining confidence in higher ed across all political groups
stances.quote: Todd can blame higher ed for being under "attack" all he wants, but perceptions of higher ed have tanked among Republicans, independents *and* Democrats, albeit from different starting points. Only 50% of Democrats have confidence in higher ed now!

stances.summary: Critiques politicians' TV performance as atypical skill
stances.quote: IDK, I don't think she's a strong candidate, but it's not because of her affect. Of course, politicians are supposed to be better at feigning interest. But being a politician who gives great TV interviews is closer to aberrant than normal, often kind of Dark Triad-adjacent tbh.

stances.summary: Implied criticism of epidemiologists' Twitter presence
stances.quote: Looking forward to some random Sunday afternoon 3 years from now when I'm like "why do I follow like 100 epidemiologists on Twitter?"

stances.summary: Directs criticism at officials over individuals
stances.quote: I've written and deleted a version of this tweet like 12 times, but I think overall people should direct more of their ire at governmental officials and less at random dumb individuals.

stances.summary: Calls out a tweet as among worst ever posted
stances.quote: I know there's a lot of competition but this is the worst thing he's ever tweeted.

stances.summary: Criticizes employer's selective outrage over comedian's jokes
stances.quote: Hopefully they can use their investigative skills to solve the mystery of why someone they hired as a comedian told jokes. https://t.co/xWc1k1oBZK

stances.summary: Suggests removing Trump before leaving office for historical significance
stances.quote: Honestly the idea of Mike Pence being president for 12 hours or something, so that everyone who looks back at the list of U.S. Presidents generations from now is like "WTF happened there?", is another (small) reason to vote on removal *before* Trump leaves office.

stances.summary: Warns democracy is threatened if impeaching for inciting insurrection faces backlash
stances.quote: If there's a significant political backlash for impeaching Trump for **inciting an insurrection** then we're probably completely fucked no matter what.

stances.summary: Notes erosion of election-result acceptance norms is concerning but pathetic
stances.quote: It's hard to strike the right balance between, on the one hand, pointing out how the erosion of democratic norms around accepting election results is highly concerning in the long run, and, on the other hand, pointing out how desperate and pathetic this all is.

stances.summary: Criticizes DNC leadership selection as self-interested and incompetent
stances.quote: The problem is that the type of person who would want a job at the DNC is exactly the type of person that Democrats shouldn't want on the DNC. Parochial, self-interested busybodies. Lots of Peter Principle at play (limited career prospects; has risen to level of incompetence).

stances.summary: Identifies Republican leverage in Senate negotiations
stances.quote: Perhaps a bit far-fetched, but Romney actually has a decent amount of leverage, if he and one of Collins, Murkowski, etc. threatened to become "Independent Republicans" or what have you who caucused with the Democrats.

stances.summary: Iran hostilities correlate with Trump approval decline
stances.quote: Timing lines up remarkably well with gas prices and the resumption of hostilities in Iran.

stances.summary: Suggests AI capex drives GDP growth, implies legal costs inflate remaining growth
stances.quote: 60% of GDP growth in the past year is due to AI capex. The other 40% is NBA billable hours to Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

stances.summary: Condemns Haitian immigrant rhetoric as profoundly racist
stances.quote: I've been around these premises long enough that you hopefully won't mistake me for woke, but the Haitian immigrant stuff is profoundly racist and you should substantially lower your esteem for anybody engaging in it.

stances.summary: Criticizes lifetime judicial appointments as problematic
stances.quote: (Whispers: It's kind of insane to have irrevocable lifetime appointments for *anything*.)

stances.summary: Credits Parkland students for sustaining gun control momentum
stances.quote: So far, Parkland is *not* fading from the news the way that mass shootings usually do. (The graph shows Google searches for the term "gun control".) The students speaking out makes a pretty big difference. https://t.co/8IcJuJ6yTS
